Getting started

This guide gets a local SQRL environment running with the same service layout used by the containerized application.

Prerequisites

For the recommended Docker workflow, install Docker Desktop with Compose support. For split local development, install Python 3.10+, Node.js 20+, npm, PostgreSQL, and MinIO.

Run with Docker Compose

From the repository root:

Copy-Item .env.example .env
docker compose up --build -d

The stack exposes these services:

Service

Address

SQRL application

http://localhost:8000

Interactive API docs

http://localhost:8000/docs

PostgreSQL

localhost:5433

MinIO API

http://localhost:9000

MinIO console

http://localhost:9001

pgAdmin

http://localhost:5050

Check the application and follow logs:

curl http://localhost:8000/api/health
docker compose logs -f sqrl

Stop the stack with docker compose down. Use docker compose down -v only when you intentionally want to remove the local PostgreSQL and MinIO volumes.

Run the backend locally

Push-Location backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
Pop-Location

The backend expects PostgreSQL and MinIO to be available. The API is mounted under /api and the development documentation is available at /docs.

Run the frontend locally

Push-Location frontend
npm ci
npm run dev
Pop-Location

The production client uses the same-origin /api base. During local development, use the Vite proxy configuration or point the client at the running backend.

First request

  1. Register at POST /api/auth/register.

  2. Log in at POST /api/auth/login and keep the bearer token.

  3. Create a workspace and attach a data source.

  4. Inspect and preprocess the data.

  5. Train a model and use the recommended model for predictions.

Configuration

Copy .env.example before starting the application. Important settings include DATABASE_URL, MINIO_ENDPOINT, MINIO_BUCKET, TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, SQUIRREL_CONNECTOR_SECRET_KEY, and CORS_ORIGINS. Provider credentials are required only for the providers used by the assisted workflow.
